examples.purpose: A paid payment: the word and the Paid mode set together, for a green tick beside “Paid · 21 Oct 2026”.

from.quote: A green tick: the money went through.

examples.purpose: A request that ran out: Expired is the default mode, so the line sets no mode and shows a grey “!”.

from.quote: Expired, the default, a grey “!”.

examples.purpose: Payments in a thread: each TransactionBubble ends with its own status line, so the words go in the bubble's status and date and the Transaction Status mode is set on the bubble.
examples.jsx:
<VStack alignHorizontal="flex-end">
  <TransactionBubble
    style={{ width: 231, maxWidth: '100%' }}
    description="Paid to Priya Sharma"
    value="1,200"
    status="Paid"
    date="21 Oct 2026"
    modes={{ 'Transaction Status': 'Paid' }}
  />
  <TransactionBubble
    style={{ width: 231, maxWidth: '100%' }}
    description="Request to Rahul Verma"
    value="450"
    status="Requested"
    date="Today"
    modes={{ 'Transaction Status': 'Request' }}
  />
  <TransactionBubble
    style={{ width: 231, maxWidth: '100%' }}
    description="Payment to Uber India"
    value="56"
    status="Declined"
    date="20 Mar 2025"
    modes={{ 'Transaction Status': 'Declined' }}
  />
</VStack>

from.quote: Set the Transaction Status mode on the bubble, as in Figma: the bubble passes its modes to the line, and its status and date props give the words.

props.name: status
props.description: With status left out the word follows the mode (its copy token), except Request, which still shows “Expired” beside an orange “!” (the token's copy, kept by Marcin's decision). Declared: Status text, e.g. "Expired". Defaults to `transactionStatus/copy` for the active mode.

props.name: date
props.description: Date text, e.g. "20 Mar 2025". Default "20 Mar 2025", from the component source.

props.name: style
props.description: style goes last on the root. The line takes no onPress, accessibility props, testID, or rest props. Declared: Optional container style.

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: The mark stays 18 × 18 when the line is cut (a 120 px column and row, a 200 px VStack) and when disableTruncation lets the text wrap. Declared: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

modes.name: Transaction Status
modes.description: Picks the mark at 18 × 18: Request an orange “!”, Paid a green tick, Declined a red cross, Expired a grey “!”. With no mode the line is the Expired mode: a grey “!” beside “Expired · 20 Mar 2025”. Declared: A token collection TransactionStatus reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

gaps.text: Figma's Transaction Status line ends in a chevron; in the package the chevron belongs to TransactionBubble, so a TransactionStatus on its own has none.
In Figma the mode picks the icon, the colour and the word together; in the package the mode picks the mark, and status and date are free text, so code passes the word.
The Coin Components Library has no Transaction Status: it is a Coin Subcomponents part that designers meet inside Transaction Bubble.
